name: Houmt Souk
tagline: The island's main town and its market
description: The principal town on the northern coast, built around a covered market, a set of fondouks converted into hotels and the Borj El Kebir fort on the water. It is the only genuinely walkable part of the island and where the everyday business of Djerba happens.
bestFor: Anyone without a vehicle or wanting a town rather than a resort
pros: The only walkable centre on the island
Markets, banks and services all here
cons: No swimmable beach in the town itself
Busy and touristy in the covered souk
Quiet out of season with much closed

name: Erriadh and Djerbahood
tagline: The old village painted by artists from thirty countries
description: An inland village south of Houmt Souk, home to the El Ghriba synagogue and, since 2014, to the Djerbahood project that brought street artists from around the world to paint its whitewashed walls. It is quiet, residential and the most interesting place on the island to wander.
bestFor: Anyone drawn to the street art and the island's Jewish heritage
cons: No beach and no restaurants to speak of
Security presence around the synagogue at times

name: Sidi Mahrez and the Zone Touristique
tagline: The hotel strip along the northeast beach
description: The long stretch of hotels along the island's best beach on the northeastern shore, built for European package tourism and largely self-contained. The sand and water here are the best on Djerba and almost nothing outside the hotels serves residents.
pros: The best beach and water on the island
Hotel facilities and the most reliable internet
cons: Expensive relative to the rest of Djerba
Much of it closes out of season

name: Midoun
tagline: The island's second town, inland and local
description: A working town in the east of the island with a Friday market that fills the streets, ordinary shops and a local rhythm that the coast has lost. It sits a few kilometres back from the resort strip and rents are a fraction of what the beach costs.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting local prices with the beach a short drive away
pros: Much cheaper than the coastal strip
Friday market and real local commerce
Ten minutes from the eastern beaches

name: Aghir
tagline: The quieter beaches on the southeast shore
description: The southeastern coast towards the Roman causeway, with quieter beaches, a scattering of smaller hotels and the flamingo lagoon nearby in winter. It is calmer than the main hotel strip and closer to the road across to the mainland.
bestFor: Anyone wanting a beach without the package-tourism density
pros: Quieter beaches than the northeast strip
Flamingos on the lagoon in winter
Closest to the causeway to the mainland
cons: A car is needed for anything
Some stretches of shore are seaweed-heavy
